newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle owners were pricing cattle at $66 to $67 per cwt on Monday while packers were bidding $64, feedlot sources said.
The bulk of trade last week was at $64.
"Packers are bidding steady money at $64 and acting like they are very comfortable with inventory. We sold them a lot of cattle last week," a Kansas cattle feeder said.
USDA reported 133,500 head traded in Texas/west Oklahoma last week and 103,700 head in Kansas.
"I think it will be Wednesday before we see any trade," another Kansas source noted.
There were mixed reports about how quickly cattle purchased last week were being picked up, with some reporting a fast pace while others saying the rate was just normal.
"I won't say it is real quick right now. It is not like they turned around and picked up everything but they have picked up two or three loads a day," one Texas cattle feeder said.
There were also reports that packers were shipping cattle from Texas, where supplies appear particularly plentiful, and moving them north to locations in Kansas and Colorado.
